title: How to Get Rid of Ants Naturally (Garden and Kitchen)
hook: A line of ants marching across your kitchen counter? You don't have to spray chemicals around your food and pets. Seven natural steps to find them, block them and keep them out, indoors and in the garden. Stay for step three: it erases the trail they follow.
intro: Ants follow invisible scent trails left by scouts, so one crumb can bring a whole colony. To stop them for good, remove what attracts them, erase their trails, and block the ways in. Keep oils, powders and cleaners away from pets and children, and never mix products.
youNeedNarration: You'll need white vinegar and water in a spray bottle, food-grade diatomaceous earth, a tube of caulk for cracks, and a soapy sponge. Keep essential oils away from pets.
heroImagePrompt: A line of small black ants walking along a kitchen counter edge toward a few crumbs, macro photo, shallow depth of field, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Find the trail and the entry point
steps.narration: Step one. Don't kill the ants you see, at least at first. Follow the line, and watch where they come from and where they go. This shows you the entry point, which could be a crack in a window frame, a gap under a door or a hole around a pipe. It also shows you what they want, such as a sugary spill or pet food. Knowing the source lets you fix the cause, rather than chasing the symptoms every week. Take a photo if you can, because it helps you remember the route.
steps.tip: Follow the trail before you spray
steps.mistake: Spraying the ants you see and nothing else
steps.imagePrompt: A line of ants entering a small crack along a kitchen window frame, macro, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Clean up food and water sources
steps.narration: Step two. Wipe all counters, tables and floors. Clean up sticky spills, crumbs and grease. Store sugar, honey, flour and cereal in airtight containers, and put pet food away after meals. Fix leaking taps and wipe sinks dry at night. Ants need water too. Empty your trash often, and rinse recycling. A clean kitchen removes the reward, and the ants will gradually give up and look elsewhere. Check under appliances and inside cupboards too, where crumbs and moisture often hide.
steps.mistake: Leaving pet food bowls out overnight
steps.imagePrompt: A hand wiping a kitchen counter with a sponge near an airtight jar of sugar, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Erase the scent trails
steps.narration: Step three. Mix equal parts white vinegar and water in a spray bottle. Spray it on the ants' trail, and wipe the area with a cloth, then repeat along the whole route, including the entry point. Vinegar breaks down the scent markers the ants use to find their way, so scouts get confused. Use soapy water as an alternative, which also kills ants on contact. Do this daily for a few days. Avoid spraying vinegar on natural stone counters. Always wear gloves, and ventilate the room, since a strong vinegar smell can bother some people.
steps.imagePrompt: A spray bottle of vinegar solution being sprayed along an ant trail on a kitchen floor, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Seal the entry points
steps.narration: Step four. Once you know where the ants enter, close the gap. Use silicone caulk to fill cracks around windows, doors, baseboards and pipes. Fit weatherstripping on doors, and repair damaged window screens. Seal small holes in the wall around cables. Doing this is a long-term fix. Without entry points, the ants cannot return, however many scouts come by. Let the caulk dry completely before moving on. Use a flashlight to check dark corners, since ants like to hide behind skirting boards and cabinets.
steps.tip: A sealed gap is a permanent fix
steps.mistake: Only wiping up without sealing cracks
steps.imagePrompt: A caulk gun sealing a small gap along a window frame with a white bead of silicone, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Use natural deterrents
steps.narration: Step five. Ants dislike certain smells and barriers. Draw a line of ground cinnamon, black pepper or used coffee grounds across their path. Wipe doorways with lemon juice. A thin line of food-grade diatomaceous earth is a natural option, because it dries out the insects that cross it. Use it where it stays dry, and avoid breathing the dust. Reapply after rain or cleaning. These methods block rather than kill, so combine them with the previous steps. Keep pets out of the area while the powder is down, and clean up after a few days.
steps.tip: Thin lines work better than piles
steps.imagePrompt: A thin line of ground cinnamon along a door threshold on a tile floor, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Deal with ants in the garden
steps.narration: Step six. Outdoors, ants often farm aphids on your plants. Rinse the aphids away with a strong spray of water, or with soapy water, and the ants will lose interest. Sprinkle food-grade diatomaceous earth around the plants and along the nest entrance on a dry day. Pour very hot, not boiling, water onto a nest in a paved area, away from plant roots. Keep mulch thin near the house, and trim any branches touching the walls. Do this in the morning, when the ground is cool, and check again the next day.
steps.tip: Remove aphids and the ants leave
steps.mistake: Pouring hot water near plant roots
steps.imagePrompt: A small ant nest mound in garden soil next to a green plant with a gloved hand holding a watering can, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Stay consistent, know when to call
steps.narration: Step seven. Natural methods need repeating for a week or two. Keep wiping trails and reapplying barriers. Check for new entry points after heavy rain. If you see large ants with winged forms, sawdust near wood, or a colony that keeps returning, it could be carpenter ants or another structural problem, so call a pest control professional. Prevention is the key. Keep the kitchen clean, the cracks sealed and the garden tidy. Keep a notebook of where and when ants appear, because patterns will tell you where to look.
steps.imagePrompt: A tidy clean kitchen counter with a sealed jar and a spray bottle, bright morning light, photorealistic, no text

bonus.label: NOT WORKING?
bonus.title: If the ants keep coming
bonus.narration: If ants keep coming back, they probably have another way in. Watch for a second trail, and check damp spots, such as under sinks and around window frames. Ants love moisture, so fix any leak. Look outside too, because plants or branches touching the wall act as bridges. Keep wiping with vinegar every day for a week or two. A new trail only means another entry point to close.
bonus.tip: A new trail is a new entry point
bonus.imagePrompt: A thin line of small black ants walking along a white window frame and sill, a hand holding a damp cloth nearby. Photorealistic photograph for a home how-to video. Bright, tidy home interior, soft daylight. Adult hands, no face visible. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: PRO TIPS
bonus.title: Identify your ants
bonus.narration: Knowing which ants you have makes the fix easier. Look at the size, the color and how they move. Take a clear photo of a few ants, or tape one to a card. A local garden center or pest control service can often identify them from a photo. Note where and when you see them, such as at night in the kitchen. That record helps you, or a pro, decide where to focus.
bonus.imagePrompt: A magnifying glass held over a few small black ants on a kitchen counter, the ants sharply in focus, a smartphone camera pointing at them. Photorealistic photograph for a home how-to video. Bright, tidy home interior, soft daylight. Adult hands, no face visible. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: PREVENTION
bonus.title: Keep ants out for good
bonus.narration: Trim branches and shrubs that touch the walls. Move mulch and firewood a few inches away from the foundation. Keep trash can lids shut, and rinse recycling before you store it. Empty the pet water bowl at night, and wipe up pet food. Inside, check the fruit bowl and the corners of the pantry each week. Ants only stay where they find something to eat.
bonus.tip: Cut off food, water and bridges
bonus.imagePrompt: Pruning shears trimming a shrub branch that touches the outside wall of a house, a clear gap left between the plants and the wall. Photorealistic photograph for a home how-to video. Sunny backyard garden, natural light. Adult hands, no face visible. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

mistakesToAvoid.narration: Here are the mistakes to avoid. First, spraying the visible ants without removing the food source. More will come. Second, using strong chemicals or essential oils around pets and children. Even natural products can be harmful in the wrong place. And third, giving up too early. Natural methods work through repetition, so keep it up for at least a week. If the problem keeps growing, there may be a nest in your wall. Also remember that the ants you see are only a small part of the colony, so the real fix is cutting off their supply. Be patient, be consistent, and be careful around pets.
items: Ignoring the food and water source
Using oils or powders near pets

recap.narration: Let's recap. Find the trail and the entry point. Clean up food and water sources. Erase the scent trails with vinegar. Seal the entry points. Use natural deterrents like cinnamon or diatomaceous earth. Deal with ants and aphids in the garden. And be consistent, and know when to call a professional. Seven steps, no harsh chemicals, and a kitchen that stays ant free. Remove, erase, block, and repeat. Bonus sections cover what to do if the ants keep coming, how to identify them, and how to keep them out for good.
items: Find the trail and the entry point
Clean up food and water sources
Deal with ants in the garden
Stay consistent, know when to call

outro: That's how you get rid of ants naturally, in the kitchen and the garden. If your counters are ant free, subscribe to WikiTube, because we publish a new how-to every single day. Tell us in the comments where your ants were coming from, and what you would like us to explain next. See you tomorrow. Don't forget to share this with a friend who has an ant problem.

metadata.title: How to Get Rid of Ants in Your House (Without Spraying Chemicals Near Food)
metadata.description:
Ants in the kitchen or the garden? In this step-by-step video you'll learn how to get rid of ants naturally: find the trail and entry point, clean up food and water sources, erase scent trails with vinegar, seal entry points with caulk, use natural deterrents like cinnamon and food-grade diatomaceous earth, deal with aphids and nests in the garden, and know when to call a professional. No harsh pesticides.

You'll need: white vinegar and water, a spray bottle, food-grade diatomaceous earth, caulk, a soapy sponge.

short.title: Ants keep coming back? Do this #shorts

short.hook: Ants keep coming back? You're removing the ants, not the trail.

steps.title: Remove the food
steps.narration: One. Wipe crumbs and spills, and store sweet food in airtight containers.

steps.title: Vinegar spray
steps.narration: Two. Spray equal parts vinegar and water on the trail, and wipe it away.

steps.title: Seal the gap
steps.narration: Three. Find where they come in, and seal it with caulk.
